lesson_scope: Principle of conservation of linear momentum with directional sign conventions; determining whether particles rebound or continue in their initial direction; calculating unknown masses and unknown post-impact speeds; collisions where one body is brought to rest; impulse calculations on rebounding bodies; secondary impacts and pursuit conditions; kinetic energy loss in rebound collisions.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Magnitude of impulse during wall rebound

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Magnitude of impulse during wall rebound

hints: Because the particle rebounds, its velocity changes sign: take right as positive, so $u = +5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v = -3\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Assign a positive direction and identify initial and final velocities:
Let motion to the right be positive:
$$u = +5\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad v = -3\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Apply the impulse formula:
$$I = m(v - u)$$

Evaluate the impulse and state its magnitude:
$$I = 0.4(-3 - 5) = 0.4(-8) = -3.2\text{ N s}$$
The magnitude of the impulse is:
$$|I| = 3.2\text{ N s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Track initial and final momentum vectors:
- Initial momentum:
$$p_i = 0.4 \times (+5) = +2.0\text{ N s}$$
- Rebound momentum:
$$p_f = 0.4 \times (-3) = -1.2\text{ N s}$$

Calculate impulse magnitude:
- Impulse is change in momentum:
$$I = p_f - p_i = -1.2 - 2.0 = -3.2\text{ N s}$$
- The barrier exerts a leftward impulse of magnitude:
$$|I| = 3.2\text{ N s}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies impulse-momentum equation with opposite signs for velocities: $I = m(v - u)$ with $u = +5$ and $v = -3$ (or $u = -5$ and $v = +3$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 2: Velocity when target particle is brought to rest

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Velocity when target particle is brought to rest

hints: Take the initial direction of $A$ as positive: $u_A = +4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $u_B = -2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. After impact, $v_B = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up conservation of linear momentum taking the initial direction of $A$ as positive:
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$
Substitute $m_A = 0.5\text{ kg}$, $u_A = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $m_B = 0.3\text{ kg}$, $u_B = -2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $v_B = 0$:
$$0.5(4) + 0.3(-2) = 0.5 v_A + 0.3(0)$$

Solve for $v_A$:
$$2.0 - 0.6 = 0.5 v_A \implies 1.4 = 0.5 v_A$$
$$v_A = \frac{1.4}{0.5} = 2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The positive sign indicates $A$ continues in its original direction of motion.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate initial total momentum:
- Particle $A$ momentum: $0.5 \times (+4) = +2.0\text{ N s}$
- Particle $B$ momentum: $0.3 \times (-2) = -0.6\text{ N s}$
- Net momentum:
$$p_{\text{total}} = 2.0 - 0.6 = +1.4\text{ N s}$$

Assign post-collision momentum to particle $A$:
- Particle $B$ is stationary, so $A$ carries all remaining momentum:
$$0.5 v_A = 1.4 \implies v_A = 2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Particle $A$ moves at $2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in its original direction.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies conservation of linear momentum with $u_A = +4$, $u_B = -2$, and $v_B = 0$: $0.5(4) + 0.3(-2) = 0.5 v_A + 0$.
Solves $2.0 - 0.6 = 0.5 v_A \implies 1.4 = 0.5 v_A$ to obtain $v_A = 2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in the original direction of $A$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 3: Finding unknown mass from rebound of striking particle

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Finding unknown mass from rebound of striking particle

hints: Because $P$ rebounds, its final velocity has the opposite sign to its initial velocity: $u_P = +6$ and $v_P = -2$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up conservation of linear momentum taking initial direction of $P$ as positive:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$$
Substitute $u_P = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $u_Q = 0$, $v_P = -2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $v_Q = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$m(6) + 0.4(0) = m(-2) + 0.4(5)$$

Rearrange and solve for $m$:
$$6m = -2m + 2.0$$
$$6m + 2m = 2.0 \implies 8m = 2.0 \implies m = \frac{2.0}{8} = 0.25\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Account for momentum change of $P$ and $Q$:
- $Q$ gains momentum:
$$\Delta p_Q = 0.4 \times 5 = 2.0\text{ N s}$$
- $P$ rebounds, so its momentum changes by:
$$\Delta p_P = m(-2 - 6) = -8m$$

Equate momentum change to zero:
$$-8m + 2.0 = 0 \implies 8m = 2.0 \implies m = 0.25\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies conservation of linear momentum with rebound sign $v_P = -2$: $m(6) + 0 = m(-2) + 0.4(5)$.
Solves $6m = -2m + 2.0 \implies 8m = 2.0$ to obtain $m = 0.25\text{ kg}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Striking particle brought to rest after rebound collision

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Striking particle brought to rest after rebound collision

hints: Take the initial direction of $A$ as positive. Particle $B$ reverses direction, so its final velocity is positive: $v_B = +2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Define the positive direction as the initial direction of $A$:
$$u_A = +3\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad u_B = -7\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Since $B$ rebounds, its velocity reverses to positive:
$$v_B = +2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$

Substitute numerical values and solve for $v_A$:
$$0.6(3) + 0.2(-7) = 0.6 v_A + 0.2(2)$$
$$1.8 - 1.4 = 0.6 v_A + 0.4$$
$$0.4 = 0.6 v_A + 0.4 \implies 0.6 v_A = 0 \implies v_A = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate momentum before and after impact:
- Total initial momentum:
$$p_i = 0.6(3) + 0.2(-7) = 1.8 - 1.4 = +0.4\text{ N s}$$
- Rebounding particle $B$ final momentum:
$$p_{B,f} = 0.2 \times (+2) = +0.4\text{ N s}$$

Find velocity of $A$:
- Conservation gives:
$$p_{A,f} = p_i - p_{B,f} = 0.4 - 0.4 = 0\text{ N s}$$
$$v_A = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Particle $A$ is brought to a complete standstill.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up momentum conservation with $u_A = +3$, $u_B = -7$, and $v_B = +2$: $0.6(3) + 0.2(-7) = 0.6 v_A + 0.2(2)$.
Solves $1.8 - 1.4 = 0.6 v_A + 0.4 \implies 0.4 = 0.6 v_A + 0.4 \implies 0.6 v_A = 0$ to obtain $v_A = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Substitute $u_P = +6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $u_Q = 0$, $v_P = -2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $v_Q = +4\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$m(6) + 0.8(0) = m(-2) + 0.8(4)$$

Rearrange to solve for $m$:
$$6m = -2m + 3.2$$
$$8m = 3.2 \implies m = \frac{3.2}{8} = 0.4\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Analyze the momentum exchange:
- Momentum gained by stationary particle $Q$:
$$\Delta p_Q = 0.8 \times 4 = 3.2\text{ N s}$$
- Rebound momentum change of $P$:
$$\Delta p_P = m(-2 - 6) = -8m$$

Solve for the mass $m$:
$$8m = 3.2 \implies m = 0.4\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies conservation of linear momentum with rebound sign $v_P = -2$: $m(6) + 0.8(0) = m(-2) + 0.8(4)$.

hints: The impulse exerted on $Q$ equals its final momentum since it started from rest: $I = m_Q v_Q$.

walkthrough.text:
State the impulse-momentum relation for particle $Q$:
$$I = m_Q v_Q - m_Q u_Q$$
Since particle $Q$ was initially at rest, $u_Q = 0$.

Substitute known values to determine $I$:
$$I = 0.8 \times 4 - 0 = 3.2\text{ N s}$$

$$I = 0.8 \times 4 = 3.2\text{ N s}$$

Verify with particle $P$:

$$|\Delta p_P| = 0.4 \times 8 = 3.2\text{ N s}$$
Both particles experience equal and opposite impulses of magnitude $3.2\text{ N s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies impulse formula $I = \Delta p_Q = m_Q v_Q - 0$ (or $\Delta p_P = |m(v_P - u_P)|$).
Calculates $I = 0.8 \times 4 = 3.2\text{ N s}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Problem 4: Particle rebound coupled with sliding across a rough horizontal floor

hints: Find the deceleration of $Q$ due to friction: $F_r = \mu mg \implies a = \mu g$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ where final velocity is zero and $s = 2.5\text{ m}$.
Solve $0 = u^2 - 2(3.2)(2.5)$ for the post-impact speed of $Q$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the deceleration of particle $Q$ on the rough horizontal floor:
$$R = mg, \quad F_r = \mu R = \mu mg$$
Applying Newton's second law in the horizontal direction:
$$F_r = ma \implies \mu mg = ma \implies a = \mu g = 0.32 \times 10 = 3.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply the constant acceleration formula with stopping distance $s = 2.5\text{ m}$ and final speed $v_f = 0$:
$$v_f^2 = u_Q^2 - 2as$$
$$0 = u_Q^2 - 2(3.2)(2.5) = u_Q^2 - 16.0$$
$$u_Q = \sqrt{16.0} = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Analyze the deceleration on the rough section:
- Sliding friction force on mass $m$:
$$F_r = 0.32m(10) = 3.2m\text{ N}$$
- Acceleration by Newton's second law:
$$a = \frac{F_r}{m} = 3.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Determine initial speed on entering the rough floor:
- Kinematic equation:
$$0^2 = u_Q^2 - 2(3.2)(2.5) = u_Q^2 - 16$$
$$u_Q = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Particle $Q$ leaves the collision with speed $4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertical forces on rough floor to find friction $F_r = \mu R = 0.32 mg$ and acceleration $a = \mu g = 0.32(10) = 3.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies suvat equation $v_f^2 = u_Q^2 - 2as$ with $v_f = 0, a = 3.2$, and $s = 2.5$.
Solves $0 = u_Q^2 - 2(3.2)(2.5) \implies u_Q^2 = 16.0$ to show $u_Q = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
